Exact K-fold cross-validation of an ordinal fit

Source: R/fb_kfold.R
fb_kfold.Rd

Refits the model once per fold with that fold's responses held out, and scores each held-out group by its log predictive density, the group's rows taken jointly. With group naming the plot, a plot is scored by the probability of all of its plants' categories together, which is how ordinal models of sub-sampled field trials are compared when leave-one-out approximations are unreliable.

Usage

fb_kfold(fit, folds, group = NULL, n_draws = 1000L, seed = NULL, ...)

Arguments

fit

An ordinal fit, from flexybayes() with family = "cumulative" or "cratio".

folds

The fold of each row of the data the fit was given: a vector with one label per row and at least two distinct labels.

group

The name of a column of the fit's data whose levels are scored jointly, for example the plot, or NULL (the default) to score each row on its own. The rows of a group must share a fold.

n_draws

The number of posterior draws per fold. Default 1000.

seed

An integer seed, or NULL (the default) to use the session's random number stream. Fold f uses seed + f.

...

Further arguments of fb_refit() for each fold's refit, for example control on brms.

Value

An object of class fb_kfold, a list with estimates, a data frame holding elpd and its standard error se, pointwise, one row per scored group with group, fold, n_rows and elpd, and folds, engine and group.

Details

On INLA a fold's responses are set to missing and its rows kept, so every latent node, an AR1 field's included, stays in the model, and the held-out linear predictors are drawn from the refit's joint posterior. On brms the model is refitted to the other folds' rows, and a held-out group's random effect at a level the refit did not see is drawn from its fitted variance (brms's allow_new_levels = TRUE with sample_new_levels = "gaussian").

The score of group g is log(mean over draws s of prod over its rows i of P(y_i | draw s)), the elpd is the sum over groups, and its standard error is sqrt(G) * sd(score) over the G groups. Rows with a missing response are not scored.

Every category must keep a training observation in every fold, or the refit would have fewer thresholds than the model it is scored against.

References

Cao Z, Megirian R, Nguyen M, Sparks AH (2026). Bayesian ordinal analysis of cereal growth stage data from oat trials in Western Australia. arXiv:2610.37384.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("INLA", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(1)
  d <- data.frame(
    trt = factor(rep(c("a", "b"), each = 60)),
    plot = factor(rep(1:24, each = 5))
  )
  eta <- 0.8 * (d$trt == "b") + rnorm(24, 0, 0.5)[d$plot]
  d$score <- cut(eta + rlogis(120), c(-Inf, -0.5, 0.5, 1.5, Inf),
    labels = c("low", "mid", "high", "top"), ordered_result = TRUE)
  fit <- flexybayes(score ~ trt, random = ~plot, data = d,
    family = "cumulative", backend = "inla", verbose = FALSE)
  folds <- rep(rep(1:4, 6), each = 5)
  fb_kfold(fit, folds, group = "plot", seed = 1L)
}
